boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Hamilton College customs, from signing the College Register to closing spring classes with a charter-day convocation.

cards.title: Sign Into Hamilton History
cards.subtitle: New students add their names to the College Register in Kirkland Cottage.
cards.notes: When your class matriculates, look closely at the historic setting before signing the register that marks the start of your Hamilton membership.
cards.short_summary: A signature in a historic cottage formally opens each new student's Hamilton story.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that, since 1975, each new student has signed the College Register in Kirkland Cottage to symbolize matriculation.
cards.access_notes: Participation is associated with new-student matriculation; follow the College's orientation instructions.

cards.title: Walk Around the Bronze Map
cards.subtitle: Campus lore warns that stepping across the central bronze map jeopardizes graduation.
cards.notes: Pause at the bronze map and follow the customary route around it; the graduation warning is documented as tradition, not fact.
cards.short_summary: One patch of bronze turns an ordinary campus walk into a graduation superstition.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton documents a tradition that students who walk across the bronze map in the center of campus will not graduate.
cards.access_notes: Observe the map from the surrounding walkway and follow posted campus-access guidance.

cards.title: Finish Spring With Three Sports
cards.subtitle: Hamilton's sprint triathlon combines a swim, bicycle leg, and 5K run.
cards.notes: Check the official event details before entering, then prepare for all three legs: a 525-yard swim, nine-mile ride, and 5K run.
cards.short_summary: The last weekend of spring classes becomes a compact swim-bike-run challenge.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton describes HamTrek as its sprint triathlon, comprising a 525-yard swim, nine-mile bicycle leg, and 5K run on the last weekend of spring classes.
cards.access_notes: The tradition coincides with the last weekend of spring classes; confirm current registration and participation requirements.

cards.title: Graduate With a Tricorn-Headed Cane
cards.subtitle: Each graduating senior receives a cane tied to Hamilton-Oneida Academy history.
cards.notes: At graduation, inspect the cane's tricorn-shaped head and connect its design to Baron von Steuben and the academy cornerstone.
cards.short_summary: A miniature Continental hat crowns Hamilton's distinctive farewell gift to seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton states that each graduating senior receives a cane whose head forms a Continental tricorn honoring Baron von Steuben, who laid the academy cornerstone.
cards.access_notes: The cane is awarded to graduating seniors; follow Commencement instructions for distribution.

cards.title: Put Academic Integrity in Writing
cards.subtitle: Hamilton students sign a pledge against dishonesty in academic work.
cards.notes: Read the pledge carefully when it is presented, then treat the signature as an ongoing commitment throughout your coursework.
cards.short_summary: A signed promise makes academic integrity a personal Hamilton obligation.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton reports that students have signed its Honor Code since 1912, pledging to abstain from dishonesty in all academic work.
cards.access_notes: This is a student academic commitment; consult current College guidance for the signing process and code requirements.

cards.title: Answer Winter With FebFest
cards.subtitle: A cold-season campus celebration built from a changing program of activities.
cards.notes: Review the year's schedule and choose a posted activity; Hamilton notes that past programs have ranged from snow sculpture to concerts.
cards.short_summary: Hamilton breaks up the cold season with a flexible festival that changes from year to year.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton identifies FebFest as a winter campus tradition and says events have included snow sculpture contests, snoccer, tastings, cook-offs, and concerts.
cards.access_notes: Activities vary by year; use the current College schedule and follow each event's stated eligibility and location guidance.

cards.title: End Classes With Charter-Day Honors
cards.subtitle: The last day of spring classes brings a history-minded convocation and awards.
cards.notes: Attend the convocation ready to hear a Hamilton-focused address and recognize the announced student and faculty prize recipients.
cards.short_summary: Hamilton's charter anniversary and final class day meet in one ceremonial gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton says Class & Charter Day began in 1950 and is a last-day-of-spring-classes convocation featuring a history-and-traditions address and awards.
cards.source_title: History of Class & Charter Day - Hamilton College
cards.access_notes: The convocation is held on the last day of spring classes; consult the current event page for venue and attendance details.

cards.title: Share One Final Week as a Class
cards.subtitle: Graduating students organize time together before Commencement.
cards.notes: Use the official senior schedule to plan your final class activities and preserve time for required Commencement preparation.
cards.short_summary: The graduating class organizes a final stretch together before the formal ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton describes Senior Week as organized by members of the graduating class and as a final opportunity for seniors to spend time together before Commencement.
cards.access_notes: Programming is for the graduating class; follow the official senior and Commencement schedules for current details.

cards.title: Light the Village as Fall Winds Down
cards.subtitle: Hamilton celebrates light across cultural and faith traditions as a symbol of hope.
cards.notes: Check the current event announcement, then join the shared reflection on what light represents across different cultural and faith traditions.
cards.short_summary: A shared light-centered gathering closes the fall semester on a hopeful note.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton's current Student Activities page identifies Lighting of Our Village as a signature tradition; an official photo retrospective says the annual event celebrates light across cultural and faith traditions.
cards.access_notes: The event occurs as the fall semester winds down; verify the current date, venue, and participation guidance in College announcements.

cards.title: Take Fall Fest Off the Hill
cards.subtitle: A Hamilton tradition links the campus community with an event in Clinton.
cards.notes: Watch Student Activities announcements for the next edition, then follow the posted location, transportation, and participation instructions.
cards.short_summary: This paired fall tradition deliberately turns attention from College Hill toward Clinton.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton's current Student Activities page explicitly identifies Fall Fest/Off the Hill Challenge among the office's long-standing traditions.
cards.source_title: What's Happening on Campus - Hamilton College Student Activities
cards.access_notes: The source does not provide a current date or venue; consult Student Activities announcements before attending.
